data.name: Meva
data.gender_notes: Meva is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Sanskrit, Meva means gentle breeze. This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'meva,' which translates to wind. In Hindu mythology, Meva is also associated with the god Vayu, the lord of the winds. The name Meva carries the meaning “Gentle Breeze” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Meva usually hope their child will grow to embody gentle breeze and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the gentle flow of life, bringing serenity and peace.
data.etymology: Meva belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gentle Breeze.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Meva total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Meva holds a unique cultural significance in the Hindu tradition. In Hindu mythology, it is believed that the deity Vayu, the god of winds, is the bearer of life-giving winds. The name Meva, which means gentle breeze or wind, is often given to children born during a calm and peaceful time, symbolizing prosperity, good luck, and a positive start to life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Meva holds deeper significance. It is believed that the name is an invocation of the grace and gentleness of the god Vayu. Hindu scriptures suggest that the body is a temple, and the breath is the spark of the divine. The name Meva serves as a reminder that every breath we take is a gift from the divine and that our lives are sustained by the gentle breeze of the universe. In this way, the name Meva serves as a constant reminder of the divine presence and the interconnectedness of all creation.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Meva, meaning 'mine' in Sanskrit, symbolizes the deep understanding of one's true self and the realization that all belongings, experiences, and emotions are an extension of that self. It is a reminder to value and cherish the inner self above material possessions.

historical_references.reference: Meva was an important Jain Tirthankara or spiritual teacher, who lived around 527-487 BCE. He is regarded as the 24th Tirthankara in the Jain tradition. Meva is also known as Mahavira, which means 'great hero', and his teachings are encapsulated in the Agamas and the Sutras.

The term 'Meva' is also used in Hinduism, particularly in the context of the Bhavishya Purana, a Hindu scripture. In this text, Meva is described as the name of a demon, who was a powerful asura (demon) and was killed by Lord Vishnu in the form of Matsya Avatar (Fish Incarnation). This event is believed to have taken place around the beginning of the Dwapara Yuga (around 3100 BCE).

In Indian fashion, designers and brands are using unique names for their collections and 'Meva' is one such name that has been gaining traction. Lastly, in spirituality, the name 'Meva' has been gaining popularity in various yoga and meditation communities, representing the divine self and inner wisdom.
